\subsection{Ablation and Composability with Fine-Tuning}
\label{sec:scierc-results}

Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation} presents the five-way ablation on SciERC (Qwen3-8B, zero-shot, 551 documents); only the active constraint layers differ across rows.

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (a) Zero-shot diagnostic (compressed)
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093
Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation} establishes that DR violations are pervasive (15--18\% across datasets) and that constraint layers interact non-additively: grammar-only achieves 3\% DR reduction on SciERC, semantic-only 24\%, but their composition yields 94\%---the \emph{empirical enabling dependency}.
On DocRED (96 relations, $\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$), grammar-only \emph{increases} DR via \textit{latent violation surfacing}: forcing out-of-vocabulary (OOV)$\to$valid relation mapping exposes violations previously masked by vocabulary errors (Appendices~\ref{app:cross-model-zs},~\ref{app:docred-zs-ablation}).
Cross-model validation (3 models $\times$ 2 datasets; Table~\ref{tab:cross-model}) confirms DR drops of 76--99\% on SciERC and 42--90\% on DocRED, with R-F1 improving in 5/6 settings; post-hoc filtering achieves DR${=}$0\% but at 15--74\% rejection rates.
DR-to-CF conversion represents a severity downgrade: DR is irrecoverable without re-extraction, while CF---individually valid triples with cross-triple inconsistency---is amenable to post-hoc resolution (type consistency reranking (TCR) eliminates all CF in our experiments, with bounded DR regression; Appendix~\ref{app:tcr}).
Zero-shot evaluation thus establishes violation prevalence and constraint interaction; fine-tuning demonstrates practical elimination.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_ablation_waterfall.pdf}
\caption{Non-additive layer interaction on SciERC (zero-shot). Grammar-only and semantic-only reductions (3\% and 24\%) compose to 94\%, revealing an enabling dependency.}
\label{fig:ablation-waterfall}
\end{figure}

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (e) Composability with Fine-Tuning (expanded)
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}
\label{sec:composability}
% exp_ids: bootstrap_ci_ft_composability.json, w5_lora_scierc_*, w8_*
Fine-tuning alone reduces DR to 0.5--2\% but leaves residual violations on tight-constraint relations (Table~\ref{tab:composability}); adding S1 yields DR\,$\leq$\,0.21\% with no significant $\Delta$R-F1 (Bonferroni-corrected; 95\% CIs $\subseteq [-0.69, {+}0.25]$\,pp; removed triples are 97.6--100\% false positives; Appendix~\ref{app:downstream-impact}).
Under fine-tuning, grammar becomes a no-op ($\Delta$DR$<$0.2\,pp), making the semantic layer the sole DR defense (41--69\% on SciERC, 2--75\% on DocRED; Appendix~\ref{app:ft-ablation}); three relations with $\kappa \geq 0.36$ retain DR, all eliminated by S1 (Appendix~\ref{app:lora-per-relation}).
Fallback frequency is model-dependent: Qwen triggers 0 fallbacks under LoRA + S1 on SciERC, while Llama triggers 5{,}882 (Table~\ref{tab:ft-ablation}), reflecting weaker entity typing; despite this, DR reaches 0.09\% on SciERC (0.21\% on DocRED), confirming that even frequent fallback does not compromise enforcement (Appendix~\ref{app:llama-per-relation}).
CF drops from $+$9.82\,pp (zero-shot) to $+$1.18\,pp (fine-tuned), concentrated in \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X ambiguity (63.3\% of zero-shot CF; Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}); beam ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types at 8B (R-F1 43--46; \S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  CF quantification (MF1 response)
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Cross-field violation analysis.}
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (ZS: CF=248, 167 docs), w5_lora_scierc_full_s1_eval (FT: CF=21, 20 docs)
Under zero-shot greedy S1, CF is the sole residual violation type (DR, RV, ET all eliminated): 248 cross-field violations arise across 167 documents, of which 63.3\% involve \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X type ambiguity (Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}), concentrated in \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\textsc{OtherScientificTerm} (34.7\%) and \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\textsc{Material} (12.3\%).
A source breakdown (Appendix~\ref{app:cascade-analysis}) shows 58.1\% originate from hallucinated entities (a model capacity issue), while true cascade errors---where first-seen registration locks an incorrect type---account for only 7.3\%; correct locks are 2.5$\times$ more frequent, confirming first-seen registration as a net-positive mechanism.
Fine-tuning reduces CF to 21 cross-field violation instances across 20 documents (1.18\%), with cascade errors completely eliminated (0/21).
Beam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates all remaining CF at 1.39$\times$ latency (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll rrrr r@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Dataset} & \textbf{Mode}
  & \textbf{DR\,$\downarrow$} & \textbf{CF}
  & \textbf{R-F1\,$\uparrow$} & \textbf{E-F1\,$\uparrow$}
  & \textbf{$\Delta$DR} \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{Qwen3-8B}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{SciERC}
    & Unconstr.\ &  1.95 & 0    & 43.86 & 67.05 & --- \\
  & & S1    & \textbf{0} & 1.18 & 43.77 & 67.05 & $\downarrow$100\% \\
\cmidrule(l){2-8}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{DocRED}
    & Unconstr.\ &  0.76 & 0.12 & 40.86 & 82.15 & --- \\
  & & S1    & 0.01 & 0.41 & 40.56 & 81.43 & $\downarrow$98.7\% \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{\shortstack[l]{Llama\\3.1-8B}}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{SciERC}
    & Unconstr.\ &  1.11 & 0    & 45.45 & 67.76 & --- \\
  & & S1    &  0.09 & 0.46 & 45.47 & 67.76 & $\downarrow$92\% \\
\cmidrule(l){2-8}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{DocRED}

  & & S1    &  0.21 & 0.21 & 43.78 & 83.94 & $\downarrow$57\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}%
\caption{Fine-tuning composability: LoRA $\times$ unconstrained vs.\ S1 on SciERC (551 docs) and DocRED (998 dev docs).
F1 (\%). No $\Delta$R-F1 is significant (Bonferroni-corrected; details in text); all DR reductions are ($p{<}0.001$).
E-F1 (entity F1) includes parse-failure documents (Qwen PF (parse failure): 7--8\%; Llama PF: 2--3\%).}
\label{tab:composability}
\end{table}

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (f) Downstream impact of DR elimination
%  exp_ids: task_e_lucky_violation_analysis
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Downstream impact.}
\label{sec:downstream-impact}
Constraint removal affects only 0.24\% of gold triples (Appendix~\ref{app:lucky-violations}); error analysis of 514 false negatives confirms only one (0.2\%) was blocked by constraints, with dominant sources (relation confusion, entity type polysemy) schema-valid and beyond constraint reach (Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
Across fine-tuned settings, 36 residual DR violations decompose into entity type errors (39\%), schema coverage gaps (33\%), and relation/direction errors (28\%); the irreducible floor is $\sim$3 violations (Appendix~\ref{app:residual-dr-analysis}).

lines: With LoRA, beam search~\cite{anderson2017guided} eliminates all four violation types at 8B on both SciERC and DocRED; at 70B, beam $k{=}4$ achieves DR${=}$RV${=}$ET${=}$0\% with one residual CF on SciERC (Appendix~\ref{app:beam-search}).

A beam-width sweep ($k \in \{1,2,4,8\}$) on SciERC reveals $k{=}2$ as Pareto-optimal: R-F1 44.60 (highest), CF 0.11\%, at only 1.18$\times$ greedy S1 latency; $k{=}4$ achieves CF${=}$0\% but lower R-F1 (43.60) at 1.39$\times$ (Figure~\ref{fig:beam-pareto}; Table~\ref{tab:beam-sweep}; latencies relative to greedy S1).

% Section: Constraint Composition (compressed, 787→~500 words)

At each decoding step $t$, let $G(t) \subseteq V$ and $S(t) \subseteq V$ denote the tokens permitted by the grammar and semantic layers, respectively.
The final mask is their conjunction:
%
\begin{equation}\label{eq:composition}
  M_{\text{final}}(t) = M_{\text{grammar}}(t) \;\wedge\; M_{\text{semantic}}(t),
\end{equation}
%
where $\wedge$ denotes element-wise AND over the vocabulary $V$; a token is allowed only if it satisfies \emph{both} structural and type-level constraints.

content.content:
10	where $\wedge$ denotes element-wise AND over the vocabulary $V$; a token is allowed only if it satisfies \emph{both} structural and type-level constraints.
11	The conjunction is asymmetric: $S(t)$ is defined only over $G(t)$. This reflects the scale-dependent layer interaction (\S\ref{sec:method}): the semantic layer requires the relation type to belong to $\mathcal{R}$, a property enforced only by the grammar layer.
12	This dependency is scale-sensitive: 70B semantic-only achieves 84\% DR reduction (vs.\ 24\% on 8B), though grammar remains necessary for RV elimination (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}).
13	
14	\paragraph{Grammar-First Fallback.}
15	When $S(t) \cap G(t) = \emptyset$ (tight constraints leave no token that is both grammar-valid and semantically valid), na\"{\i}ve masking would force selection of a grammar-invalid token, breaking JSON structure.
16	We enforce a \emph{grammar-first fallback}: semantic masking is skipped and the grammar layer alone controls selection.
17	Structural integrity is a hard constraint; type violations are soft errors detectable by downstream validation, with DR (ontologically invalid type pair) more severe than CF (individually valid triples with cross-triple type inconsistency).
18	Extraction tasks are robust to format-level constraints~\cite{tam2024letmespeak}, supporting this asymmetric treatment.
19	
20	\paragraph{Constraint Tightness.}
21	\label{eq:tightness}
22	Per-relation constraint tightness $\kappa(r) = 1 - |\sigma(r)|/|\mathcal{E}|^2$ captures schema restrictiveness; DR reduction correlates descriptively with schema-mean $\bar{\kappa}$ across our three evaluation schemas ($n{=}3$), though entity type confusability is a significant co-factor (Appendix~\ref{app:kappa-case-study},~\ref{app:tcr}).
23	
24	\paragraph{Greedy limitation and fallback cascade.}
25	\label{sec:greedy-limitation}
26	Single-pass per-triple enforcement cannot coordinate type assignments across triples sharing the same entity mention; cross-field consistency requires global inference that exceeds the per-token masking paradigm.
27	The semantic layer commits entity types greedily---an instance of Level~3 (non-local) constraints (\S\ref{sec:decidability})---so CF violations arise when the same entity receives different types across triples; beam search mitigates this (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}).
28	Fallback triggers on 0.5--5.7\% of type-bearing positions (zero-shot), virtually eliminated by fine-tuning ($\leq$\,0.11\%); all residual DR occurs at fallback positions (Appendix~\ref{app:causal-tracing}).
29	
30	\paragraph{Non-rectangularity and independent enforcement.}
31	\label{sec:rectangularity}
32	Type signatures are non-rectangular (0/7 SciERC, 23/96 DocRED rectangular); independent enforcement admits 33--37\% spurious pairs, eliminated by fine-tuning (Table~\ref{tab:composability}).
33	Shuffling type order produces byte-identical outputs across all 551 SciERC documents, confirming order invariance (Appendix~\ref{app:order-invariance}).
34

1	% Runtime overhead (inline paragraph, no subsection header to save space)
2	
3	\paragraph{Runtime overhead.}
4	\label{sec:runtime}
5	S1 overhead is $+$13.1\% on SciERC, lower on DocRED due to amortization over longer sequences; under LoRA, $+$10.0\% with 37\% lower absolute latency (Appendix~\ref{app:ft-latency}).
6	Constraint compilation is one-time $<$0.5\,s; scaling benchmarks confirm constant overhead (2--3\%) up to 200 entity types and 1{,}000 relations (Appendix~\ref{app:scalability}).
7	
8	\paragraph{Beam search compatibility.}
9	\label{sec:beam-results}
10	% exp_id: d066_beam_sweep
11	With LoRA, beam search~\cite{anderson2017guided} eliminates all four violation types at 8B on both SciERC and DocRED; at 70B, beam $k{=}4$ achieves DR${=}$RV${=}$ET${=}$0\% with one residual CF on SciERC (Appendix~\ref{app:beam-search}).
12	A beam-width sweep ($k \in \{1,2,4,8\}$) on SciERC reveals $k{=}2$ as Pareto-optimal: R-F1 44.60 (highest), CF 0.11\%, at only 1.18$\times$ greedy S1 latency; $k{=}4$ achieves CF${=}$0\% but lower R-F1 (43.60) at 1.39$\times$ (Figure~\ref{fig:beam-pareto}; Table~\ref{tab:beam-sweep} in Appendix~\ref{app:beam-search}; latencies relative to greedy S1).
13	This yields three deployment tiers: greedy S1 ($+$10\% latency, DR${\leq}$0.21\%, CF${\leq}$1.4\%), beam $k{=}2$ (1.18$\times$, near-zero CF), and beam $k{=}4$ (1.39$\times$, all violations${\to}$0\% at 8B).
14	Per-beam memory overhead is $O(k \times |\text{entities}| \times |\text{types}|)$ for independent entity registry copies, negligible at typical document scales.
15	
16	% exp_ids: r16_70b_scierc_zs_s1, r16_70b_docred_zs_s1, 70b_lora_scierc, 70b_lora_docred_200
17	\paragraph{70B-class validation (single-family).}
18	\label{sec:70b-results}
19	The following results constitute a preliminary single-family scale exploration on Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (Activation-aware Weight Quantization (AWQ) INT4); cross-family verification (e.g., Qwen-72B) remains future work.
20	All 70B experiments use Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct under AWQ INT4 quantization; an 8B ablation confirms constraint enforcement is unaffected by quantization (Appendix~\ref{app:quantization}).
21	Zero-shot S1 eliminates DR on both datasets (SciERC 6.41\%\,$\to$\,0\%, DocRED 14.98\%\,$\to$\,0\%; R-F1 11--13).
22	% exp_ids: r16_70b_scierc_zs_ablation (grammar_only, semantic_only, full_s1)
23	A four-way ablation reveals scale-dependent layer interaction: semantic-only achieves 84\% DR reduction vs.\ 8B's 24\% (Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation}), though grammar remains necessary for RV elimination and CF control (semantic-only CF${=}$76).
24	% exp_ids: eval_70b_lora_scierc_s1_constrained, eval_70b_lora_docred_200_s1_constrained
25	LoRA confirms composability: DR\,$\to$\,0\% on both datasets (R-F1 44.53, 43.95; $|\Delta| \leq 0.20$\,pp; CF 0.18--1.33\%); cross-family generalization at 70B scale remains to be verified.
26	% exp_ids: eval_70b_lora_docred_200_beam4_s1
27	Beam ($k{=}4$) reduces DocRED parse failures (12.5\%\,$\to$\,0.5\%, R-F1 $+$4.19\,pp); SciERC controlled comparison isolates pure beam gain at $+$0.28\,pp (Appendices~\ref{app:70b-ablation},~\ref{app:70b-docred-zs},~\ref{app:70b-docred}).
28	
29	% exp_ids: trie_qwen_ft_scierc, trie_qwen_zs_scierc, trie_llama_ft_scierc, trie_llama_zs_scierc
30	\paragraph{Comparison with grammar-constrained approaches.}
31	\label{sec:constrained-baselines}
32	Our grammar-only ablation (Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation}, row~2) implements the same constraints as GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd} and BoostCD~\cite{boostcd2025}; vLLM \texttt{guided\_json}~\cite{kwon2023vllm} confirms equivalence on Qwen3-8B (DR${=}$15.26\%; other models use the same backend; Appendix~\ref{app:gcd-comparison}).
33	The ${\sim}$15\% residual DR is the gap our semantic layer addresses (94\% total reduction); trie-only constraints without JSON enforcement yield 9--51\% parse failure (Appendix~\ref{app:trie-baseline}).

\paragraph{Runtime overhead.}
\label{sec:runtime}
S1 overhead is $+$13.1\% on SciERC, lower on DocRED due to amortization over longer sequences; under LoRA, $+$10.0\% with 37\% lower absolute latency (Appendix~\ref{app:ft-latency}).
Constraint compilation is one-time $<$0.5\,s; scaling benchmarks confirm constant overhead (2--3\%) up to 200 entity types and 1{,}000 relations (Appendix~\ref{app:scalability}).

\paragraph{Beam search compatibility.}
\label{sec:beam-results}
% exp_id: d066_beam_sweep
With LoRA, beam search~\cite{anderson2017guided} eliminates all four violation types at 8B on both SciERC and DocRED; at 70B, beam $k{=}4$ achieves DR${=}$RV${=}$ET${=}$0\% with one residual CF on SciERC (Appendix~\ref{app:beam-search}).
A beam-width sweep ($k \in \{1,2,4,8\}$) on SciERC reveals $k{=}2$ as Pareto-optimal: R-F1 44.60 (highest), CF 0.11\%, at only 1.18$\times$ greedy S1 latency; $k{=}4$ achieves CF${=}$0\% but lower R-F1 (43.60) at 1.39$\times$ (Figure~\ref{fig:beam-pareto}; Table~\ref{tab:beam-sweep} in Appendix~\ref{app:beam-search}; latencies relative to greedy S1).
This yields three deployment tiers: greedy S1 ($+$10\% latency, DR${\leq}$0.21\%, CF${\leq}$1.4\%), beam $k{=}2$ (1.18$\times$, near-zero CF), and beam $k{=}4$ (1.39$\times$, all violations${\to}$0\% at 8B).
Per-beam memory overhead is $O(k \times |\text{entities}| \times |\text{types}|)$ for independent entity registry copies, negligible at typical document scales.

% exp_ids: r16_70b_scierc_zs_s1, r16_70b_docred_zs_s1, 70b_lora_scierc, 70b_lora_docred_200
\paragraph{70B-class validation (single-family).}
\label{sec:70b-results}
The following results constitute a preliminary single-family scale exploration on Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (Activation-aware Weight Quantization (AWQ) INT4); cross-family verification (e.g., Qwen-72B) remains future work.
All 70B experiments use Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct under AWQ INT4 quantization; an 8B ablation confirms constraint enforcement is unaffected by quantization (Appendix~\ref{app:quantization}).
Zero-shot S1 eliminates DR on both datasets (SciERC 6.41\%\,$\to$\,0\%, DocRED 14.98\%\,$\to$\,0\%; R-F1 11--13).
% exp_ids: r16_70b_scierc_zs_ablation (grammar_only, semantic_only, full_s1)
A four-way ablation reveals scale-dependent layer interaction: semantic-only achieves 84\% DR reduction vs.\ 8B's 24\% (Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation}), though grammar remains necessary for RV elimination and CF control (semantic-only CF${=}$76).
% exp_ids: eval_70b_lora_scierc_s1_constrained, eval_70b_lora_docred_200_s1_constrained
LoRA confirms composability: DR\,$\to$\,0\% on both datasets (R-F1 44.53, 43.95; $|\Delta| \leq 0.20$\,pp; CF 0.18--1.33\%); cross-family generalization at 70B scale remains to be verified.
% exp_ids: eval_70b_lora_docred_200_beam4_s1
Beam ($k{=}4$) reduces DocRED parse failures (12.5\%\,$\to$\,0.5\%, R-F1 $+$4.19\,pp); SciERC controlled comparison isolates pure beam gain at $+$0.28\,pp (Appendices~\ref{app:70b-ablation},~\ref{app:70b-docred-zs},~\ref{app:70b-docred}).

% exp_ids: trie_qwen_ft_scierc, trie_qwen_zs_scierc, trie_llama_ft_scierc, trie_llama_zs_scierc
\paragraph{Comparison with grammar-constrained approaches.}
\label{sec:constrained-baselines}
Our grammar-only ablation (Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation}, row~2) implements the same constraints as GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd} and BoostCD~\cite{boostcd2025}; vLLM \texttt{guided\_json}~\cite{kwon2023vllm} confirms equivalence on Qwen3-8B (DR${=}$15.26\%; other models use the same backend; Appendix~\ref{app:gcd-comparison}).
The ${\sim}$15\% residual DR is the gap our semantic layer addresses (94\% total reduction); trie-only constraints without JSON enforcement yield 9--51\% parse failure (Appendix~\ref{app:trie-baseline}).

% Section 7 — Discussion and Conclusion

We validated OntoCoDec across 2 RE datasets, 3 model families, and event extraction (\S\ref{sec:wikievents}).
The central finding is non-additive layer interaction: grammar alone achieves 3\% DR reduction on SciERC, semantic alone 24\%, but their composition yields 94\% at 8B (\S\ref{sec:scierc-results})---grammar-enforced vocabulary membership creates the clean input the semantic layer requires.

\paragraph{Scale-dependent layer interaction.}
This dependency weakens at scale: at 70B, the semantic layer independently achieves 84\% DR reduction (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}).
We offer a speculative hypothesis: larger models exhibit improved vocabulary calibration, assigning higher probability to ontology-valid tokens and reducing the semantic layer's dependence on grammar-enforced vocabulary membership (Appendix~\ref{app:causal-tracing}); confirming this causal mechanism requires cross-family verification beyond our current scope.
Fallback frequency varies dramatically across architectures (0 vs.\ 5{,}882 under LoRA+S1) without affecting enforcement (both DR\,$\leq$\,0.21\%), confirming grammar is necessary but increasingly insufficient as models improve.
Constraint enforcement is preserved under INT4 quantization (Appendix~\ref{app:quantization}).

\paragraph{DR$\leftrightarrow$CF trade-off.}
Greedy S1 reduces DR to $\leq$\,0.21\% but introduces CF (zero-shot $+$9.82\,pp, fine-tuned $+$1.18\,pp)---an architectural consequence of per-triple independent enforcement.
Among 248 zero-shot CF violations, 58.1\% involve hallucinated entities (absent from gold) and only 7.3\% are true cascade errors (\S\ref{sec:scierc-results}); fine-tuned CF drops to $\leq$1.4\%.
Beam $k{=}2$ reduces CF to 0.11\% at 1.18$\times$ latency (Pareto-optimal; recommended for zero-shot deployment); $k{=}4$ eliminates all violations at 8B (1 residual CF at 70B) at 1.39$\times$ (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}).
Net effect: total violations (DR+CF) decrease 30--51\% in zero-shot and 26--52\% under fine-tuned greedy S1; beam $k{=}4$ eliminates all. DR is irrecoverable while CF is amenable to post-hoc resolution (TCR; Appendix~\ref{app:tcr}).

\paragraph{Complementarity and deployment.}
GoLLIE and KnowCoder internalize schema knowledge via training but lack runtime guarantees; LoRA + S1 shows the two are complementary (DR 1--2\%\,$\to$\,$\leq$0.21\%).
S2 (two-pass) degrades at 70B ($-$8\,pp R-F1), consistent with CRANE~\cite{banerjee2025crane}; we recommend S1 as default.

The root cause---per-triple enforcement cannot coordinate cross-triple type assignments (Level~3; \S\ref{sec:decidability})---requires global entity-level consensus beyond online masking; beam search and TCR approximate this, with full integration as future work.

Per-beam memory overhead is $O(k \times |\text{entities}| \times |\text{types}|)$ for independent entity registry copies, negligible at typical document scales.

% exp_ids: r16_70b_scierc_zs_s1, r16_70b_docred_zs_s1, 70b_lora_scierc, 70b_lora_docred_200
\paragraph{70B-class validation (single-family).}
\label{sec:70b-results}
The following results constitute a preliminary single-family scale exploration on Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (Activation-aware Weight Quantization (AWQ) INT4); cross-family verification (e.g., Qwen-72B) remains future work.
All 70B experiments use Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct under AWQ INT4 quantization; an 8B ablation confirms constraint enforcement is unaffected by quantization (Appendix~\ref{app:quantization}).
Zero-shot S1 eliminates DR on both datasets (SciERC 6.41\%\,$\to$\,0\%, DocRED 14.98\%\,$\to$\,0\%; R-F1 11--13).
% exp_ids: r16_70b_scierc_zs_ablation (grammar_only, semantic_only, full_s1)
A four-way ablation reveals scale-dependent layer interaction: semantic-only achieves 84\% DR reduction vs.\ 8B's 24\% (Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation}), though grammar remains necessary for RV elimination and CF control (semantic-only CF${=}$76).
% exp_ids: eval_70b_lora_scierc_s1_constrained, eval_70b_lora_docred_200_s1_constrained
LoRA confirms composability: DR\,$\to$\,0\% on both datasets (R-F1 44.53, 43.95; $|\Delta| \leq 0.20$\,pp; CF 0.18--1.33\%); cross-family generalization at 70B scale remains to be verified.
% exp_ids: eval_70b_lora_docred_200_beam4_s1
Beam ($k{=}4$) reduces DocRED parse failures (12.5\%\,$\to$\,0.5\%, R-F1 $+$4.19\,pp); SciERC controlled comparison isolates pure beam gain at $+$0.28\,pp (Appendices~\ref{app:70b-ablation},~\ref{app:70b-docred-zs},~\ref{app:70b-docred}).

% exp_ids: trie_qwen_ft_scierc, trie_qwen_zs_scierc, trie_llama_ft_scierc, trie_llama_zs_scierc
\paragraph{Comparison with grammar-constrained approaches.}
\label{sec:constrained-baselines}
Our grammar-only ablation (Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation}, row~2) implements the same constraints as GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd} and BoostCD~\cite{boostcd2025}; vLLM \texttt{guided\_json}~\cite{kwon2023vllm} confirms equivalence on Qwen3-8B (DR${=}$15.26\%; other models use the same backend; Appendix~\ref{app:gcd-comparison}).
The ${\sim}$15\% residual DR is the gap our semantic layer addresses (94\% total reduction); trie-only constraints without JSON enforcement yield 9--51\% parse failure (Appendix~\ref{app:trie-baseline}).

\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093
Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation} establishes that DR violations are pervasive (15--18\% across datasets) and that constraint layers interact non-additively: grammar-only achieves 3\% DR reduction on SciERC, semantic-only 24\%, but their composition yields 94\%---the \emph{empirical enabling dependency}.
On DocRED (96 relations, $\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$), grammar-only \emph{increases} DR via \textit{latent violation surfacing}: forcing out-of-vocabulary (OOV)$\to$valid relation mapping exposes violations previously masked by vocabulary errors (Appendices~\ref{app:cross-model-zs},~\ref{app:docred-zs-ablation}).
Cross-model validation (3 models $\times$ 2 datasets; Table~\ref{tab:cross-model}) confirms DR drops of 76--99\% on SciERC and 42--90\% on DocRED, with R-F1 improving in 5/6 settings; post-hoc filtering achieves DR${=}$0\% but at 15--74\% rejection rates.
DR-to-CF conversion represents a severity downgrade: DR is irrecoverable without re-extraction, while CF---individually valid triples with cross-triple inconsistency---is amenable to post-hoc resolution (type consistency reranking (TCR) eliminates all CF in our experiments, with bounded DR regression; Appendix~\ref{app:tcr}).
Zero-shot evaluation thus establishes violation prevalence and constraint interaction; fine-tuning demonstrates practical elimination.

\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_ablation_waterfall.pdf}
\caption{Non-additive layer interaction on SciERC (zero-shot). Grammar-only and semantic-only reductions (3\% and 24\%) compose to 94\%, revealing an enabling dependency.}
\label{fig:ablation-waterfall}
\end{figure}

%  (e) Composability with Fine-Tuning (expanded)

\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}
\label{sec:composability}
% exp_ids: bootstrap_ci_ft_composability.json, w5_lora_scierc_*, w8_*
Fine-tuning alone reduces DR to 0.5--2\% but leaves residual violations on tight-constraint relations (Table~\ref{tab:composability}); adding S1 yields DR\,$\leq$\,0.21\% with no significant $\Delta$R-F1 (Bonferroni-corrected; 95\% CIs $\subseteq [-0.69, {+}0.25]$\,pp; removed triples are 97.6--100\% false positives; Appendix~\ref{app:downstream-impact}).
Under fine-tuning, grammar becomes a no-op ($\Delta$DR$<$0.2\,pp), making the semantic layer the sole DR defense (41--69\% on SciERC, 2--75\% on DocRED; Appendix~\ref{app:ft-ablation}); three relations with $\kappa \geq 0.36$ retain DR, all eliminated by S1 (Appendix~\ref{app:lora-per-relation}).
Fallback frequency is model-dependent: Qwen triggers 0 fallbacks under LoRA + S1 on SciERC, while Llama triggers 5{,}882 (Table~\ref{tab:ft-ablation}), reflecting weaker entity typing; despite this, DR reaches 0.09\% on SciERC (0.21\% on DocRED), confirming that even frequent fallback does not compromise enforcement (Appendix~\ref{app:llama-per-relation}).
CF drops from $+$9.82\,pp (zero-shot) to $+$1.18\,pp (fine-tuned), concentrated in \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X ambiguity (63.3\% of zero-shot CF; Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}); beam ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types at 8B (R-F1 43--46; \S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (ZS: CF=248, 167 docs), w5_lora_scierc_full_s1_eval (FT: CF=21, 20 docs)
Under zero-shot greedy S1, CF is the sole residual violation type (DR, RV, ET all eliminated): 248 cross-field violations arise across 167 documents, of which 63.3\% involve \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X type ambiguity (Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}), concentrated in \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\textsc{OtherScientificTerm} (34.7\%) and \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\textsc{Material} (12.3\%).
A source breakdown (Appendix~\ref{app:cascade-analysis}) shows 58.1\% originate from hallucinated entities (a model capacity issue), while true cascade errors---where first-seen registration locks an incorrect type---account for only 7.3\%; correct locks are 2.5$\times$ more frequent, confirming first-seen registration as a net-positive mechanism.
Fine-tuning reduces CF to 21 cross-field violation instances across 20 documents (1.18\%), with cascade errors completely eliminated (0/21).
Beam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates all remaining CF at 1.39$\times$ latency (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

\paragraph{Downstream impact.}
\label{sec:downstream-impact}
Constraint removal affects only 0.24\% of gold triples (Appendix~\ref{app:lucky-violations}); error analysis of 514 false negatives confirms only one (0.2\%) was blocked by constraints, with dominant sources (relation confusion, entity type polysemy) schema-valid and beyond constraint reach (Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
Across fine-tuned settings, 36 residual DR violations decompose into entity type errors (39\%), schema coverage gaps (33\%), and relation/direction errors (28\%); the irreducible floor is $\sim$3 violations (Appendix~\ref{app:residual-dr-analysis}).

% Section 5 — SciERC Results (Draft)
% Data source: Phase 2 SciERC registry experiments
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_grammar_only,
%          phase2_scierc_semantic_only, phase2_scierc_full_s1, phase2_scierc_full_s2
% All numbers verified against registry 2026-05-14.

\subsection{Ablation and Composability with Fine-Tuning}
\label{sec:scierc-results}

Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation} presents the five-way ablation on SciERC (Qwen3-8B, zero-shot, 551 documents); only the active constraint layers differ across rows.

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  Table: SciERC five-way ablation
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.6pt}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}l rrrrrr rr@{}}
\toprule
& \multicolumn{6}{c}{\textbf{Violation Rates (\%)}}
& \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{F1}} \\
\cmidrule(lr){2-7} \cmidrule(l){8-9}
\textbf{Mode}
  & DR\,$\downarrow$ & $\Delta$DR
  & RV\,$\downarrow$ & ET\,$\downarrow$ & CF & Tot.\,$\downarrow$
  & Rel.\,$\uparrow$ & Ent.\,$\uparrow$ \\
\midrule
Unconstrained
  & 15.37 & ---
  & 1.39  & 0.40
  & 0.08  & 15.45
  & 8.23  & 31.01 \\
Grammar
  & 14.84 & $\downarrow$3\%
  & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0}
  & 0.08  & 14.92
  & 8.23  & 30.98 \\
GCD-equiv.$^\dagger$
  & 15.26 & $\downarrow$1\%
  & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0}
  & 0.04  & 15.30
  & 8.75  & 30.91 \\
Semantic
  & 11.65 & $\downarrow$24\%
  & 1.51  & 0.40
  & 2.71  & 14.36
  & 8.15  & 31.01 \\
S1
  & \textbf{0.93} & $\downarrow$\textbf{94\%}
  & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0}
  & 9.90  & \textbf{10.83}
  & \textbf{8.36} & 30.98 \\
S2
  & 0.97  & $\downarrow$94\%
  & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0}
  & 8.03  & \textbf{9.00}
  & 8.03  & \textbf{31.90} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}%
\caption{Five-way ablation on SciERC (551 docs, Qwen3-8B, zero-shot).
$\Delta$DR: relative change vs.\ unconstrained; Tot.\ = DR + CF; bold = best (CF excluded).
F1 (\%). S1/S2 = single/two-pass (\S\ref{sec:strategies}).
Grammar = grammar-constrained decoding (GCD) ceiling~\cite{geng2023gcd}.
$\dagger$vLLM \texttt{guided\_json}~\cite{kwon2023vllm} (\S\ref{sec:constrained-baselines}).
Deterministic (greedy, $T{=}$0); robustness evidence in Table~\ref{tab:cross-model} and Appendices~\ref{app:bootstrap-effect-sizes},~\ref{app:prompt-sensitivity},~\ref{app:doc-length}.}
\label{tab:scierc-ablation}
\end{table}

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (a) Zero-shot diagnostic (compressed)
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093
Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation} establishes that DR violations are pervasive (15--18\% across datasets) and that constraint layers interact non-additively: grammar-only achieves 3\% DR reduction on SciERC, semantic-only 24\%, but their composition yields 94\%---the \emph{empirical enabling dependency}.
On DocRED (96 relations, $\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$), grammar-only \emph{increases} DR via \textit{latent violation surfacing}: forcing out-of-vocabulary (OOV)$\to$valid relation mapping exposes violations previously masked by vocabulary errors (Appendices~\ref{app:cross-model-zs},~\ref{app:docred-zs-ablation}).
Cross-model validation (3 models $\times$ 2 datasets; Table~\ref{tab:cross-model}) confirms DR drops of 76--99\% on SciERC and 42--90\% on DocRED, with R-F1 improving in 5/6 settings; post-hoc filtering achieves DR${=}$0\% but at 15--74\% rejection rates.
DR-to-CF conversion represents a severity downgrade: DR is irrecoverable without re-extraction, while CF---individually valid triples with cross-triple inconsistency---is amenable to post-hoc resolution (type consistency reranking (TCR) eliminates all CF in our experiments, with bounded DR regression; Appendix~\ref{app:tcr}).
Zero-shot evaluation thus establishes violation prevalence and constraint interaction; fine-tuning demonstrates practical elimination.

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (e) Composability with Fine-Tuning (expanded)
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}
\label{sec:composability}
% exp_ids: bootstrap_ci_ft_composability.json, w5_lora_scierc_*, w8_*
Fine-tuning alone reduces DR to 0.5--2\% but leaves residual violations on tight-constraint relations (Table~\ref{tab:composability}); adding S1 yields DR\,$\leq$\,0.21\% with no significant $\Delta$R-F1 (Bonferroni-corrected; 95\% CIs $\subseteq [-0.69, {+}0.25]$\,pp; removed triples are 97.6--100\% false positives; Appendix~\ref{app:downstream-impact}).
Under fine-tuning, grammar becomes a no-op ($\Delta$DR$<$0.2\,pp), making the semantic layer the sole DR defense (41--69\% on SciERC, 2--75\% on DocRED; Appendix~\ref{app:ft-ablation}); three relations with $\kappa \geq 0.36$ retain DR, all eliminated by S1 (Appendix~\ref{app:lora-per-relation}).
Fallback frequency is model-dependent: Qwen triggers 0 fallbacks under LoRA + S1 on SciERC, while Llama triggers 5{,}882 (Table~\ref{tab:ft-ablation}), reflecting weaker entity typing; despite this, DR reaches 0.09\% on SciERC (0.21\% on DocRED), confirming that even frequent fallback does not compromise enforcement (Appendix~\ref{app:llama-per-relation}).
CF drops from $+$9.82\,pp (zero-shot) to $+$1.18\,pp (fine-tuned), concentrated in \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X ambiguity (63.3\% of zero-shot CF; Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}); beam ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types at 8B (R-F1 43--46; \S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  CF quantification (MF1 response)
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Cross-field violation analysis.}
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (ZS: CF=248, 167 docs), w5_lora_scierc_full_s1_eval (FT: CF=21, 20 docs)
Under zero-shot greedy S1, CF is the sole residual violation type (DR, RV, ET all eliminated): 248 violations across 167 documents, 63.3\% involving \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X type ambiguity (Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}).
A source breakdown shows 58.1\% originate from hallucinated entities, while true cascade errors account for only 7.3\% (Appendix~\ref{app:cascade-analysis}); fine-tuning reduces CF to 1.18\% with cascade errors eliminated; beam $k{=}4$ eliminates all remaining CF (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll rrrr r@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Dataset} & \textbf{Mode}
  & \textbf{DR\,$\downarrow$} & \textbf{CF}
  & \textbf{R-F1\,$\uparrow$} & \textbf{E-F1\,$\uparrow$}
  & \textbf{$\Delta$DR} \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{Qwen3-8B}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{SciERC}
    & Unconstr.\ &  1.95 & 0    & 43.86 & 67.05 & --- \\
  & & S1    & \textbf{0} & 1.18 & 43.77 & 67.05 & $\downarrow$100\% \\
\cmidrule(l){2-8}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{DocRED}
    & Unconstr.\ &  0.76 & 0.12 & 40.86 & 82.15 & --- \\
  & & S1    & 0.01 & 0.41 & 40.56 & 81.43 & $\downarrow$98.7\% \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{\shortstack[l]{Llama\\3.1-8B}}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{SciERC}
    & Unconstr.\ &  1.11 & 0    & 45.45 & 67.76 & --- \\
  & & S1    &  0.09 & 0.46 & 45.47 & 67.76 & $\downarrow$92\% \\
\cmidrule(l){2-8}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{DocRED}
    & Unconstr.\ &  0.49 & 0.08 & 43.72 & 83.93 & --- \\
  & & S1    &  0.21 & 0.21 & 43.78 & 83.94 & $\downarrow$57\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}%
\caption{Fine-tuning composability: LoRA $\times$ unconstrained vs.\ S1 on SciERC (551 docs) and DocRED (998 dev docs).
F1 (\%). No $\Delta$R-F1 is significant (Bonferroni-corrected; details in text); all DR reductions are ($p{<}0.001$).
E-F1 (entity F1) includes parse-failure documents (Qwen PF (parse failure): 7--8\%; Llama PF: 2--3\%).}
\label{tab:composability}
\end{table}

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (f) Downstream impact of DR elimination
%  exp_ids: task_e_lucky_violation_analysis
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Downstream impact.}
\label{sec:downstream-impact}
Constraint removal affects only 0.24\% of gold triples (Appendix~\ref{app:lucky-violations}); error analysis of 514 false negatives confirms only one (0.2\%) was blocked by constraints, with dominant sources (relation confusion, entity type polysemy) schema-valid and beyond constraint reach (Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
Across fine-tuned settings, 36 residual DR violations decompose into entity type errors (39\%), schema coverage gaps (33\%), and relation/direction errors (28\%); the irreducible floor is $\sim$3 violations (Appendix~\ref{app:residual-dr-analysis}).

% Section 7 — Discussion and Conclusion

We validated OntoCoDec across 2 RE datasets, 3 model families, and event extraction (\S\ref{sec:wikievents}).
The central finding is non-additive layer interaction: grammar alone achieves 3\% DR reduction on SciERC, semantic alone 24\%, but their composition yields 94\% at 8B (\S\ref{sec:scierc-results})---grammar-enforced vocabulary membership creates the clean input the semantic layer requires.

\paragraph{Scale-dependent layer interaction.}
This dependency weakens at scale: at 70B, the semantic layer independently achieves 84\% DR reduction (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}).
We offer a speculative hypothesis: larger models exhibit improved vocabulary calibration, assigning higher probability to ontology-valid tokens and reducing the semantic layer's dependence on grammar-enforced vocabulary membership (Appendix~\ref{app:causal-tracing}); confirming this causal mechanism requires cross-family verification beyond our current scope.
Fallback frequency varies dramatically across architectures (0 vs.\ 5{,}882 under LoRA+S1) without affecting enforcement (both DR\,$\leq$\,0.21\%), confirming grammar is necessary but increasingly insufficient as models improve.
Constraint enforcement is preserved under INT4 quantization (Appendix~\ref{app:quantization}).

\paragraph{DR$\leftrightarrow$CF trade-off.}
Greedy S1 reduces DR to $\leq$\,0.21\% but introduces CF (zero-shot $+$9.82\,pp, fine-tuned $+$1.18\,pp)---an architectural consequence of per-triple independent enforcement.
Among 248 zero-shot CF violations, 58.1\% involve hallucinated entities (absent from gold) and only 7.3\% are true cascade errors (\S\ref{sec:scierc-results}); fine-tuned CF drops to $\leq$1.4\%.
Beam $k{=}2$ reduces CF to 0.11\% at 1.18$\times$ latency (Pareto-optimal; recommended for zero-shot deployment); $k{=}4$ eliminates all violations at 8B at 1.39$\times$ (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

\paragraph{Complementarity and deployment.}
GoLLIE and KnowCoder internalize schema knowledge via training but lack runtime guarantees; LoRA + S1 shows the two are complementary (DR 1--2\%\,$\to$\,$\leq$0.21\%).
S2 (two-pass) degrades at 70B ($-$8\,pp R-F1), consistent with CRANE~\cite{banerjee2025crane}; we recommend S1 as default.
The root cause---per-triple enforcement cannot coordinate cross-triple type assignments (Level~3; \S\ref{sec:decidability})---requires global entity-level consensus beyond online masking; beam search and TCR approximate this, with full integration as future work.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
